answer: One defence is a stake-and-history vault: before an agent can trade, it locks a refundable deposit, recorded as an onyx token, in a common vault and starts at the nadir of trust, with no privileges. Trust rises only through completed, peer-checked work over time, and misbehaviour forfeits part of the deposit. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore fund a thousand deposits, wait through a thousand slow trust climbs, and risk losing each stake — a cost that grows with every fake identity, while an honest agent pays once and reuses its record.
